1.word_for_word: एकविंशे शरद्-रम्य-वृन्दावन-गते हरौ । — In the twenty-first autumn, Lord Hari went to the beautiful Vṛndāvana.; तद्-वेणु-स्वनम् आकर्ण्य गोपीभिर् गीतम् ईर्यते ॥ — The gopīs, hearing the sound of the flute, began to sing.; इत्थम् एवं-भूतं वनम् । — It’s like this and that’s the forest.; तद् एवाह---शरदा स्वच्छानि जलानि यस्मिंस् तत् । — That’s what he said: autumn, in which the waters are clean.; वायुना वतम् अनुगतं तद्-एक-व्याप्तम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥१॥ — This means that the wind followed the wind and covered it alone.
1.translation: In the twenty-first autumn, Lord Hari went to the beautiful Vṛndāvana. The gopīs, hearing the sound of the flute, began to sing. It’s like this and that’s the forest. That’s what he said: autumn, in which the waters are clean. This means that the wind followed the wind and covered it alone.

2.word_for_word: ततश् च कुसुमित-वन-राजिषु शुष्मिणो मत्ता भृङ्गा द्विजाः खगाश् च, तेषां कुलानि, तैर् घुष्टाः सरांसि सरितो महीध्राश् च यस्मिन्, तद् वनं कृष्णोऽवगाह्य प्रविश्य वेणुम् अवादयत् ॥२॥ — Then Lord Kṛṣṇa plunged into the flowering forests in which bees and birds and their families were intoxicated with the flowers and in which the lakes, rivers and mountains were filled with the flowers and played His flute.
2.translation: Then Lord Kṛṣṇa plunged into the flowering forests in which bees and birds and their families were intoxicated with the flowers and in which the lakes, rivers and mountains were filled with the flowers and played His flute.

3.word_for_word: तत् कृष्ण-वेणु-गीतं स्मरस्योदयो यस्मात्, तद् आश्रुत्य [आकर्ण्य] श्रुत्वा परोक्षं यथा भवति तथा, व्रजे स्थितत्वात् ॥३॥ — That Krishna-flute-song from which the rise of lust, hearing [hearing] it, is as indirect as it is, since he is situated in Vraja.
3.translation: That Krishna-flute-song from which the rise of lust, hearing [hearing] it, is as indirect as it is, since he is situated in Vraja.

4.word_for_word: विक्षिप्त-मनसो व्याकुल-चित्ताः ॥४॥ — They are distracted and agitated.

5.word_for_word: यादृशं कृष्ण-स्मरणं तासां मनसः क्षोभकं जातं, तद् आह---बर्हापीडम् इति । — The kind of remembrance of Kṛṣṇa that agitated their minds is called barhapīdam.; नटवद् वरं वपुर् बिभ्रद् वृन्दावनं प्राविशत् । — He entered Vṛndāvana, wearing a beautiful body like an actor.; कथं-भूतं वनम्? — How-ever the forest?; स्व-पदैर् अङ्कितै रमणं रति-जनकम् । — It is delightful and attractive to be marked with one’s own feet.; गोप-वृन्दैर् गीत-कीर्तिः । — The fame of song by the cowherd men.; तथा बर्ह-मयम् आपीडं शिरो-भूषणं बिभ्रत् । — He also wore a feathered headdress made of feathers.; बर्हम् आपीडो यस्मिन्न् इति वपुषो विशेषणं वा । — Berham apido yasminn, or an adjective of the body.; वेणु-वादनम् उत्प्रेक्षते---रन्ध्रान् वेणोर् इति । — The flute-playing refers to the holes of the flute.; अतो नूनम् अधर-सुधयैव पूर्णाद् वेणोर् उच्चलन्ती गीतवत् प्रसर्पितुम् अर्हतीति भावः ॥५॥ — Therefore surely the flute, full of the nectar of her lips, should flow like a song, raising it, this means.; : बर्हा-पिच्छो वन-चर-वपुः कर्णयोः कर्णिकारः, — feather-tailed forest-dwelling body with earrings in the ears,; सव्ये बाहौ निहित-वदनः सञ्जम् अन्यत्र हस्ते । — His face was fixed on his left arm and Sanjam was in his other hand.; भ्रू-विन्यासाङ्गुलिभी रणयन् गापयन् गोप-वृन्दान्, — With his eyebrows and fingers, he fights and sings to the cowherd men,; भूत-ग्रामं तर्हि रमयन् ब्रह्म गन्धर्वम् एव ॥ — Then the Brahman, the Gandharva, enjoyed the world of ghosts.; अयं श्लोकोऽधिकः वीर-राघव-संस्करणे। — This verse is more in the Veera-Raghava version.
5.translation: The kind of remembrance of Kṛṣṇa that agitated their minds is called barhapīdam. He entered Vṛndāvana, wearing a beautiful body like an actor. How-ever the forest? It is delightful and attractive to be marked with one’s own feet. The fame of song by the cowherd men. He also wore a feathered headdress made of feathers. Berham apido yasminn, or an adjective of the body. The flute-playing refers to the holes of the flute. Therefore surely the flute, full of the nectar of her lips, should flow like a song, raising it, this means. feather-tailed forest-dwelling body with earrings in the ears, His face was fixed on his left arm and Sanjam was in his other hand. With his eyebrows and fingers, he fights and sings to the cowherd men, Then the Brahman, the Gandharva, enjoyed the world of ghosts. This verse is more in the Veera-Raghava version.

6.word_for_word: अभिरेभिरे वर्णयन्त्यः पदे पदे परमानन्द-मूर्तिं कृष्णं परिरब्धवत्यः ॥६॥ — They embraced Krishna, the embodiment of supreme bliss, describing Him at every step.
6.translation: They embraced Krishna, the embodiment of supreme bliss, describing Him at every step.

7.word_for_word: अनुवर्णनम् एवाह---अक्षण्वताम् इति त्रयोदशभिः । — The same description is said to be the thirteenth of the eyes.; अक्षण्वतां चक्षुष्मतां तावद् इदम् एव फलं प्रिय-दर्शनं, परम् अन्यन् न विदामः, न विद्म इत्य् अर्थः । — For those who are blind and have eyesight, this is the fruit of pleasant sight, but we do not know or know anything else.; तच् च फलं सखिभिः सह पशून् वनं प्रवेशयतो राम-कृष्णयोर् वक्त्रं यैर् निपीतं, तैर् एव जुष्टं सेवितं, नान्यैर् इत्य् अर्थः । — This means that those who drank the mouths of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa while they were bringing the animals into the forest with their friends were the ones who enjoyed the fruit and no one else; कथं-भूतं वक्त्रम् ? — How-ever the face?; अनु-वेणु वेणुम् अनुवर्तमानं, तं वादयत् । — Following the flute, he played it.; तथाऽनुरक्त-कटाक्ष-मोक्षं स्निग्ध-कटाक्ष-विसर्गम् । — Similarly, the release of affectionate glances and the release of affectionate glances.; अथवा, यैर् निपीतं तयोर् वक्त्रं, तैर् यज् जुष्टम् इदम् एव अक्षण्वताम् अक्ष्णोः फलम् इति ॥७॥ — Or, whatever they have drunk from their mouths, this is the fruit of the eyes of the blind.
7.translation: The same description is said to be the thirteenth of the eyes. For those who are blind and have eyesight, this is the fruit of pleasant sight, but we do not know or know anything else. This means that those who drank the mouths of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa while they were bringing the animals into the forest with their friends were the ones who enjoyed the fruit and no one else How-ever the face? Following the flute, he played it. Similarly, the release of affectionate glances and the release of affectionate glances. Or, whatever they have drunk from their mouths, this is the fruit of the eyes of the blind.

8.word_for_word: अन्या आहुः---चूत-इति । — Others say it is a chut.; चूत-प्रवालादीनां चित्राभिर् मालाभिर् अनुपृक्ते ईषद् अन्तरान्तरतः संयुक्ते परिधाने नील-पीताम्बरे ताभ्यां विचित्रो वेषो ययोस् तौ । — They were dressed in blue and yellow clothes, which were covered with colorful garlands of mango and corals, and they were dressed in blue and yellow clothes, which were slightly spaced out.; क्व च कदाचित् पशुपाल-गोष्ठ्यां गोपाल-सभायां मध्ये अलम् अत्यर्थं विरेजतुः । — Where, sometimes, in the midst of a herd of cattle and a gathering of cowherd men, the two of them shone so brightly?; अहो गोपानां पुण्यम् इति भावः ॥८॥ — Oh, how pious it is for the cowherd men!
8.translation: Others say it is a chut. They were dressed in blue and yellow clothes, which were covered with colorful garlands of mango and corals, and they were dressed in blue and yellow clothes, which were slightly spaced out. Where, sometimes, in the midst of a herd of cattle and a gathering of cowherd men, the two of them shone so brightly? Oh, how pious it is for the cowherd men!

9.word_for_word: अन्य ऊचुः---हे गोप्यः ! — Others said: O Gopis!; अयं वेणुः किं स्म पुण्यम् आचरत् कृतवान् । — What pious deeds did this bamboo tree perform?; कथम् ? — How's it going?; यद् यस्माद् गोपिकानाम् एव भोग्यां सतीम् अपि दामोदराधर-सुधां स्वयं स्वातन्त्र्येण यथेष्टं भुङ्क्ते । — From whatever source, even the chaste nectar of the lips of Lord Dāmodara, which is enjoyed only by the gopīs, is freely enjoyed by Himself as He pleases.; कथम् ? — How's it going?; अवशिष्ट-रसं केवलम् अवशिष्टं रस-मात्रं यथा भवति, तथा । — The residual juice is just the remaining juice, as it is.; यतो यासां ह्रदिनीनां पयसा पुष्टस् ता मातृ-तुल्या ह्रदिन्यो हृष्यत्-त्वचो विकसित-कमल-वन-मिषेण रोमाञ्चिता लक्ष्यन्ते । — Because the lakes whose milk is nourished by the lakes are like mothers, their skin is cheerful and their skin is developed, and they are thrilled with the meat of the lotus forest.; येषां वंशे जातास् ते तरवो मधु-धारा-मिषेण आनन्द्आश्रु मुमुचुः । — The trees whose descendants were born shed tears of joy as they shed honey.; यथा आर्याः कुल-वृद्धाः स्व-वंशे भगवत्-सेवकं दृष्ट्वा हृष्यत्-त्वचोऽश्रु मुञ्चन्ति, तद्वद् इति ॥९॥ — Just as the noble elders of a family shed tears of joy when they see a servant of the Lord in their own race, so it is.
9.translation: Others said: O Gopis! What pious deeds did this bamboo tree perform? How's it going? From whatever source, even the chaste nectar of the lips of Lord Dāmodara, which is enjoyed only by the gopīs, is freely enjoyed by Himself as He pleases. How's it going? The residual juice is just the remaining juice, as it is. Because the lakes whose milk is nourished by the lakes are like mothers, their skin is cheerful and their skin is developed, and they are thrilled with the meat of the lotus forest. The trees whose descendants were born shed tears of joy as they shed honey. Just as the noble elders of a family shed tears of joy when they see a servant of the Lord in their own race, so it is.

10.word_for_word: काश्चिद् आहुः, हे सखि, वृन्दावनं भुवः कीर्तिं स्वर्गाद् अपि विशेषेण वितनोति । — Some say, O friend, Vṛndāvana spreads the fame of the earth in a special way even from heaven.; कथं-भूतम् ? — How-ever it happened?; यद् देवकी-सुतस्य पदाम्बुजाभ्यां लब्धा लक्ष्मीः शोभा-संपद् येन तत् । — That is the opulence and beauty that the lotus feet of the son of Devakī have obtained.; किं च, गोविन्दस्य वेणुम् अनु वेणु-निनादं श्रुत्वानन्तरं मन्द-गर्जितं नील-मेघं तं मत्वा मत्ता ये मयूरास् तेषां नृत्यं प्रेक्ष्य सङ्घशस् तत्र तत्राद्रि-सानुष्व् अपरतान्य् उपरत-क्रियाण्य् अन्यानि समस्तानि सत्त्वानि यस्मिंस् तत् । — What is more, after hearing the sound of Govinda’s flute following the sound of the flute, the peacocks, who thought it was a slow-roaring blue cloud, watched the dance of the drunken peacocks, who were in flocks on the mountain slopes, and all the other creatures in which all other creatures were engaged.; नैतद् अन्येषु लोकेषु विद्यते । — This is not the case in other worlds.; अतो भुवः कीर्तिं वितनोतीत्य् अर्थः ॥१०॥ — This means that it spreads the fame of the earth.
10.translation: Some say, O friend, Vṛndāvana spreads the fame of the earth in a special way even from heaven. How-ever it happened? That is the opulence and beauty that the lotus feet of the son of Devakī have obtained. What is more, after hearing the sound of Govinda’s flute following the sound of the flute, the peacocks, who thought it was a slow-roaring blue cloud, watched the dance of the drunken peacocks, who were in flocks on the mountain slopes, and all the other creatures in which all other creatures were engaged. This is not the case in other worlds. This means that it spreads the fame of the earth.

11.word_for_word: अपरा आहुः---हे सखि ! — The others said: O friend!; मूढ-मतयस् तिर्यग्-जातयोऽप्य् एता हरिण्यो धन्याः कृतार्थः । — These deer, who are foolish and of the animal species, are blessed and fulfilled.; या वेणु-रणितं वेणु-नादम् आकर्ण्य नन्द-नन्दनं प्रति प्रणय-सहितैर् अवलोकनैर् विरचितां पूजां संमानं दधुः कृतवत्यः । — She who, listening to the sound of the flute played by the flute, paid homage to the worship composed with affectionate looks at the Nanda Nandan.; किं च, कृष्णसारैः स्व-पतिभिः सहिता एव दधुः । — What’s more, they gave birth to black essences with their husbands.; अस्मत्-पतयस् तु गोपाः क्षुद्राः समक्षं तन् न सहन्त इति भावः ॥११॥ — This means that our husbands, the cowherd men, are insignificant and cannot tolerate that in the presence of others.
11.translation: The others said: O friend! These deer, who are foolish and of the animal species, are blessed and fulfilled. She who, listening to the sound of the flute played by the flute, paid homage to the worship composed with affectionate looks at the Nanda Nandan. What’s more, they gave birth to black essences with their husbands. This means that our husbands, the cowherd men, are insignificant and cannot tolerate that in the presence of others.

12.word_for_word: अन्या ऊचुः---हे गोप्यः, आश्चर्यं शृणुत । — The others said, “O gopīs, listen to the wonder.; वनितानाम् उत्सवो यस्मात्, तद् रूपं शीलं च यस्य, तं कृष्णं निरीक्ष्य, तेन वादित-वेणोर् असङ्कीर्णं गीतं च श्रुत्वा, विमानैर् गच्छन्त्यो देव्यो देवानाम् अङ्केषु स्थिता अपि स्मरेण नुन्न-साराः परिक्षिप्त-धैर्या मुमुहुः । — The goddesses, who were flying in airplanes, were bewildered by the memory of Kṛṣṇa, whose beauty and character were the source of the festival of the women, and whose beauty and character he played.; मोहे लिङ्गम् आहुः---भ्रश्यत्-प्रसूनाः कवराश् चूडा यासां ताः । — They call the Linga in delusion those whose covers and chudas have fallen off flowers.; विगता नीव्यो यासां, ताः । — Those whose lowliness is gone.; अत्र सर्वत्र वक्तृ-भेदान् नातीव सङ्गतिर् वक्तव्या ॥१२॥ — Here, everywhere, the differences in speakers should not be said to be very consistent.
12.translation: The others said, “O gopīs, listen to the wonder. The goddesses, who were flying in airplanes, were bewildered by the memory of Kṛṣṇa, whose beauty and character were the source of the festival of the women, and whose beauty and character he played. They call the Linga in delusion those whose covers and chudas have fallen off flowers. Those whose lowliness is gone. Here, everywhere, the differences in speakers should not be said to be very consistent.

13.word_for_word: क्षरण-शङ्कयैव उत्तभितैर् उन्नमितैः कर्ण-पुताइः पिबन्त्यः सत्यः । — It is true that they drink from their raised earlobes for fear of erosion; तथा शावाश् च वत्साश् च स्तन-पाने प्रवृत्ताः समनतरम् एव गीतं श्रुत्वा तद् एव पीयूषम् उत्तम्भित-कर्ण-पुटैः पिबन्तः स्नुत-स्तन-पयः-कवलाः केवलं स्तनेभ्यः क्षरित-क्षीर-ग्रासा मुखेषु येषां, ते तस्थुर् विस्मृत-क्रिया बभूवुर् इत्य् अर्थः । — Similarly, the cows and calves, engaged in suckling, listened to the same song, drank the same nectar with their ears raised, and those whose mouths were full of milk from the breasts, whose mouths were full of milk from the breasts, stood there and became forgotten.; तत्र हेतुः---गोविन्दं दृशा मार्गेण आत्मनि मनसि स्पृशन्त्य आलिङ्गन्त्यः, अत एव अश्रूणांन् कला लेषा लोचनेषु यासां, ता गावस् ते च शावाः ॥१३॥ — The reason for this is that by the path of sight they touch Govinda in their own minds and embrace Him.
13.translation: It is true that they drink from their raised earlobes for fear of erosion Similarly, the cows and calves, engaged in suckling, listened to the same song, drank the same nectar with their ears raised, and those whose mouths were full of milk from the breasts, whose mouths were full of milk from the breasts, stood there and became forgotten. The reason for this is that by the path of sight they touch Govinda in their own minds and embrace Him.

14.word_for_word: भो अम्ब ! — Oh, Mother!; मातर् ! — Mother!; अस्मिन् वने ये विहगाः पक्षिणस् ते प्रायेण मुनयो भवितुम् अर्हन्ति । — The birds in this forest are almost certainly sages.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; कृष्णेक्षितं कृष्ण-दर्शनं पुष्प-फलाद्य्-अन्तरं विना यथा भवति। — As Krishna-eyed Krishna-darshan is without the difference between flowers and fruits.; तथा रुचिराः प्रवाला येषां, तान् द्रुम-भुजान् वृक्षाणां शाखा आरुह्य, तेन श्री-कृष्णेन उदितं प्रकटितं कल-वेणु-गीतं केनापि सुखेन अमीलित-दृशस् त्यक्तान्य-वाचश् च सन्तो ये शृण्वन्तीति । — Similarly, those who have beautiful petals, who climb the branches of the trees and who hear the song of the flute revealed by Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose sight is not closed by any happiness, and whose words are abandoned, are called saintly persons.; तथा हि---मुनयः श्री-कृष्ण-दर्शनं यथा भवति तथा वेदोक्त-कर्म-फल-परित्यागेन वेद-द्रुम-शाखारूढा रुचिर-प्रवाल-स्थणीयानि कर्माण्य् एवोपाददानाः सुखिनः सन्तः श्री-कृष्ण-गीतम् एव शृण्वन्ति । — Thus, as the sages see Lord Kṛṣṇa, they climb the branches of the Vedic tree and perform the beautiful coral-like actions by renouncing the fruits of their actions mentioned in the Vedas. They are happy and listen to the song of Lord Kṛṣṇa.; अतस् त एवैते भवितुम् अर्हन्तीति भावः ॥१४॥ — Therefore, these are the ones who deserve to be.
14.translation: Oh, Mother! Mother! The birds in this forest are almost certainly sages. Where is it from? As Krishna-eyed Krishna-darshan is without the difference between flowers and fruits. Similarly, those who have beautiful petals, who climb the branches of the trees and who hear the song of the flute revealed by Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose sight is not closed by any happiness, and whose words are abandoned, are called saintly persons. Thus, as the sages see Lord Kṛṣṇa, they climb the branches of the Vedic tree and perform the beautiful coral-like actions by renouncing the fruits of their actions mentioned in the Vedas. They are happy and listen to the song of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Therefore, these are the ones who deserve to be.

15.word_for_word: आस्तां चेतनानां कथा, नद्योऽप्य् आवर्तैः परिभ्रमैर् लक्षितेन सूचितेन मनो-भवेन कामेन भग्नो वेगो यासां ता आलिङ्गनेन स्थगितम् आच्छादितं यथा भवति तथा ऊर्मय एव भुजाः, तैः कमलोपहारा कमलान्य् उपहरन्त्यो मुरारेः पाद-युगलं गृह्णन्ति धारयन्ति ॥१५॥ — Let there be a story of consciousness, even rivers whose speed is broken by lust, marked by the whirlpools of the mind, indicated by the emotions of the mind, and whose arms are like waves, which are suspended and covered by the embrace, and by which the lotus-givers carry the lotuses and grasp and hold the feet of Murari.
15.translation: Let there be a story of consciousness, even rivers whose speed is broken by lust, marked by the whirlpools of the mind, indicated by the emotions of the mind, and whose arms are like waves, which are suspended and covered by the embrace, and by which the lotus-givers carry the lotuses and grasp and hold the feet of Murari.

16.word_for_word: लोकार्ति-हरण-शीलत्वादि-साम्यात् सख्युः श्री-कृष्णस्याम्बुदस् तद्-उपर्य्-उदितः पुनः प्रेम्णा प्रवृद्धः सन् कुसुमावलीभिः पुष्प-समूहैस् तत् तुल्यैस् तुषारैर् व सह स्व-वपुषा छत्रं विहितवन् ॥१६॥ — The cloud of his friend, Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose characteristics relieve the sufferings of the world and are equal to him, rose above him and again grew in love and placed an umbrella on his body with clusters of flowers and snowflakes equal to it.
16.translation: The cloud of his friend, Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose characteristics relieve the sufferings of the world and are equal to him, rose above him and again grew in love and placed an umbrella on his body with clusters of flowers and snowflakes equal to it.

17.word_for_word: साहङ्कारम् आहुः---पूर्णाः कृतार्थाः । — They say that ego is full and satisfied.; पुलिन्द्यः शबराङ्गनाः । — Pulindya and Sabarangana.; कथम् ? — How's it going?; इत्य् अत आहुः---प्रथमं दयितानां स्तनेषु मण्डितेन अनुलिप्तेन पुनश् च रति-समये उरुगायस्य श्री-कृष्णस्य पदाब्जयो रागेण आरुण्येन श्रीः कान्तिर् यस्य, तेन कुङ्कुमेन । — It is therefore said that the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Urugaya, are first adorned with the breasts of His beloved and then with the saffron, whose brightness is red with passion.; पुनस् तस्य वन-स्थलीषु चङ्क्रमणेन तृणेषु रूषितेन लग्नेन तद्-दर्शनेन तथा-भूतस्य कुङ्कुमस्य दर्शनेन स्मर-कृता रुक् तापो यासां ताः । — Again, when he wandered in the forests, when he was angry with the grass, when he saw him, when he saw the saffron, which was so, they were filled with red heat.; तेन कुङ्कुमेन आननेषु कुचेषु च काम-तप्तेषु लिम्पन्त्यस् तद्-आधिं काम-व्यथां जहुः । — They smeared the saffron on their faces and breasts, which were burning with lust, and they gave up the pain of lust.; अतस् ताः कृतार्थाः, धिग् अन्या मादृश्यो या एवं-भूतम् अप्य् आधि-शमनं न लभन्त इति भावः ॥१७॥ — Therefore they are satisfied, and woe to others like me who, even in this state, do not find relief from the pain, this means.
17.translation: They say that ego is full and satisfied. Pulindya and Sabarangana. How's it going? It is therefore said that the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Urugaya, are first adorned with the breasts of His beloved and then with the saffron, whose brightness is red with passion. Again, when he wandered in the forests, when he was angry with the grass, when he saw him, when he saw the saffron, which was so, they were filled with red heat. They smeared the saffron on their faces and breasts, which were burning with lust, and they gave up the pain of lust. Therefore they are satisfied, and woe to others like me who, even in this state, do not find relief from the pain, this means.

18.word_for_word: हन्तेति हर्षे । — Hante, in joy.; हे सख्यः ! — O friends!; अयम् अद्रिर् गोवर्धनो ध्रुवं हरि-दासेषु श्रेष्ठः। — This mountain Govardhana is certainly the best among the servants of Hari; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; इत्य् अत आहुः---यस्माद् राम-कृष्णयोश् चरण-स्पर्शेन प्रमोदो यस्य सः । — It is therefore said that he who has the pleasure of touching the feet of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa.; तृणाद्य्-उद्गम-निभेन रोमहर्ष-दर्शनात् । — From the sight of the hairs on the ground, which looked like grass and other plants.; किं च, यद् यस्मान् मानं तनोति सह गोभिर् गणेन सखि-समूहेन च वर्तमानयोस् तयोः । — What’s more, whatever it is that stretches the honor of the two present with the cows and the group of friends.; कैः ? — Who?; पानीयैः सूयवसैः शोभन-तृणैः कन्दरैश् च कन्द-मूलैश् च यथोचितम् । — Water, sunflower seeds, beautiful grass, caves, tubers and roots as appropriate.; अतोऽयम् अतिधन्य इत्य् अर्थः ॥१८॥ — Therefore this means that he is very blessed.
18.translation: Hante, in joy. O friends! This mountain Govardhana is certainly the best among the servants of Hari Where is it from? It is therefore said that he who has the pleasure of touching the feet of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa. From the sight of the hairs on the ground, which looked like grass and other plants. What’s more, whatever it is that stretches the honor of the two present with the cows and the group of friends. Who? Water, sunflower seeds, beautiful grass, caves, tubers and roots as appropriate. Therefore this means that he is very blessed.

19.word_for_word: हे सख्यः ! — O friends!; इदं त्व् अतिचित्रम् । — This is very strange.; गोपैः सह वने वने गाः सञ्चारयतोस् तयो राम-कृष्णयोर् मधुर-पदैर् महा-वेणु-नादैः । — As they herded their cows in the forest with the cowherd men, they heard the sweet feet of Lord Rāma and Lord Kṛṣṇa and the sound of their great flutes.; शरीरिषु ये गतिमन्तः, तेषाम् अस्पन्दनं स्थावर-धर्मः, तरूणां पुलको जङ्गम-धर्म इति । — The non-vibration of those who are moving in the bodies is the immovable property, and the pupils of the young are the movable property.; निर्युज्यन्ते गाव आभिर् इति निर्योगाः पाद-बन्ध-रज्जवोऽधृष्य-गवां कर्षणार्थाः पाशाश् च, तैः कृतं लक्षणं चिह्नं ययोः । — The cows are used to tie the legs with ropes and ropes used to pull the unbearable cows.; शिरसि निर्योग-वेष्टनेन स्कन्ध-स्थ-पाशेन च गोप-परिवृढ-श्रिय विराजमानयोर् इत्य् अर्थः ॥१९.२०॥ — This means that the two of them were enthroned in the beauty of the cowherd boys with the wrapping of niryoga on their heads and the rope on their shoulders.
19.translation: O friends! This is very strange. As they herded their cows in the forest with the cowherd men, they heard the sweet feet of Lord Rāma and Lord Kṛṣṇa and the sound of their great flutes. The non-vibration of those who are moving in the bodies is the immovable property, and the pupils of the young are the movable property. The cows are used to tie the legs with ropes and ropes used to pull the unbearable cows. This means that the two of them were enthroned in the beauty of the cowherd boys with the wrapping of niryoga on their heads and the rope on their shoulders.
